featured_reviews.name: Nitesh shelke
featured_reviews.review_text:
I came across this beautiful Nandi Bull Statue near Plaza Cinema in Dadar East. It’s a striking and culturally symbolic statue that represents strength, patience, and devotion in Indian mythology. The statue is beautifully crafted and placed right in the middle of a bustling area, making it a peaceful yet eye-catching spot.

It adds a unique charm to the area and is perfect for a quick photo stop while exploring Dadar. The surrounding area is lively with theatres, local shops, and classic Mumbai street vibes. A great example of tradition blending with city life.

Tip: Visit in the evening when the traffic calms down a bit, and the lighting makes the statue look even more majestic.

featured_reviews.name: Nishad Shahasane
featured_reviews.review_text:
Plaza Cinema is one of Mumbai’s oldest and most famous movie halls, located in the heart of Dadar, just a 5-minute walk from Dadar Station and near Shivsena Bhavan.

It’s a single-screen theatre with around 800 seats and a classic, nostalgic charm. The screen is big, the sound is good, and the hall is clean. Facilities include clean washrooms, drinking water, and parking for cars and bikes (no roadside parking).

Snacks are slightly expensive but easily available. The place is usually crowded, which adds to its lively atmosphere. There is a bus stop nearby named "Plaza" from where you can find BEST buses to various locations across Mumbai.

Overall, Plaza Cinema offers a good, old-school movie experience at affordable prices — a must-visit for anyone who loves vintage theatres.

On a rainy Sunday, I visited Nakshatra Mall in Dadar West and the experience was quite pleasant. Located conveniently near Shivaji Park, the mall is easy to reach and offers a cozy escape from the rains. Though not as large as some of the newer malls in the city, Nakshatra Mall has its own charm with a compact layout and a good mix of shopping, dining, and entertainment options.

The mall houses a variety of retail outlets, including popular apparel and lifestyle stores, making it a convenient spot for casual shopping. It also has a few branded showrooms where one can find both everyday wear and festive collections. What I particularly liked was that the mall wasn’t overcrowded, which made the shopping experience more comfortable, especially on a rainy day when people usually prefer indoor activities.

The food court and small eateries provide enough options for a quick bite, from snacks to proper meals. The seating area was neat, and the service was reasonably quick. The cinema hall inside the mall is another highlight, offering a good option to catch a movie while spending time indoors.

Overall, Nakshatra Mall may not be very big, but it is well-maintained, convenient, and a good weekend hangout spot.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Citylight Cinema for a Sunday evening show recently. Overall, the theatre experience was actually not bad. For around ₹400, we got two tickets for a weekend evening show, which felt quite reasonable. The theatre was also pretty packed, so clearly a lot of people visit this place regularly.

The main disappointment was the food section. They had a large variety of items displayed on the menu screens, but most of them were not available. Only popcorn, samosas, nachos, and a paneer tikka sandwich were being served. Nothing else from the menu seemed available.

If you’re displaying so many food options, especially during a busy weekend evening show when people are likely to snack more, the counters should be better stocked. It creates unnecessary disappointment when customers see multiple items advertised but can’t actually order them.

Overall: decent theatre experience and fair ticket pricing, but the food availability definitely needs improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Krittika Khandare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing this review to document a serious food safety incident at PVR, Jio World Plaza, BKC.

On 15 January 2026, I attended the 6:00 PM show of Avatar 3 in Audi 6. Before the movie, I purchased food from the PVR counter. While eating it during the show, the final bite contained a visible piece of glass that entered my mouth. I immediately spat it out. The fact that I was not physically injured was purely a matter of luck, this could have caused severe internal injury or worse.

I have video evidence clearly showing the glass shard in the food.

What has been equally disturbing is the way this matter has been handled since. Despite multiple emails, follow-ups, and assurances that the issue was being taken seriously, there were significant delays, inconsistent communication, and ultimately a response stating that no lapse could be established at their end. The only gesture initially offered was complimentary movie tickets, which is entirely inappropriate for a life-threatening food safety incident.

As a paying customer, being exposed to such a risk and then experiencing weeks of delay and deflection has been deeply distressing. This review is being posted so that other patrons are aware and so that this concern is documented publicly after private escalation failed to lead to a responsible resolution.

I hope PVR reviews its food safety accountability and customer handling practices more seriously going forward.

The theatre itself was extremely clean, the seats were very comfortable, and the cooling was VERY strong — honestly, carry a jacket if you’re planning to watch a movie there because it gets quite cold inside. The overall ambience and maintenance were excellent.

Ticket pricing between ₹250–₹500 feels reasonable considering the cleanliness and comfort, especially if booked smartly on weekdays.

But as usual with PVR, the food pricing is absurd. Ordered a ₹350 Schezwan Paneer Wrap and it was a complete waste of money. The taste was terrible and definitely not worth the price. They serve it properly with a tray, plate, and cutlery, but realistically, how convenient is that setup inside a movie theatre while watching a film in the dark?

Popcorn and drinks are also heavily overpriced, and the quantity doesn’t justify the cost either.

Overall: great theatre experience for seating, cleanliness, and ambience — but avoid spending too much on the food unless you’re okay paying premium prices for average quality.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My recent experience at the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand in Dadar left me with mixed feelings. While the overall service of the Shivneri buses remains commendable, the facilities at the bus stand itself are in dire need of improvement, particularly when it comes to providing adequate shelter and comfort for passengers.

On a rainy day, I found myself at the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand, eagerly waiting for my bus. Unfortunately, my anticipation was quickly dampened, both literally and figuratively, as the facility failed to offer proper protection from the elements. The absence of sufficient shelter made it difficult for passengers to find a dry spot to stand or sit, leaving many of us exposed to the rain. It was disheartening to see elderly passengers and families with children struggling to stay dry while waiting for their buses.

The lack of proper infrastructure at the bus stand was evident. The limited seating arrangements were inadequate for the number of passengers present, and those available were often wet due to the rain. There were no covered waiting areas or even basic shelters to shield passengers from the weather. This situation is particularly concerning during the monsoon season when rain is frequent and heavy in Mumbai. A bus stand as busy and important as Dadar's Shivneri should certainly prioritize the comfort and convenience of its passengers by providing better infrastructure.

Despite these shortcomings, there are several positive aspects to note about the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand. The staff at the stand were courteous and helpful, assisting passengers with their queries and providing timely updates about bus arrivals and departures. The ticketing process was efficient, and I appreciated the digital screens displaying real-time information about bus schedules. This helped in reducing the anxiety of waiting, as passengers could see exactly when their buses were expected to arrive.

Additionally, the cleanliness of the bus stand was maintained reasonably well. Despite the rain, the staff made efforts to keep the area free of litter, which is commendable. The security presence was also reassuring, ensuring that passengers felt safe while waiting for their buses.

However, the positive aspects cannot entirely overshadow the critical need for better facilities. For an otherwise excellent service like Shivneri, enhancing the infrastructure at the Dadar bus stand is essential. Investing in covered waiting areas, more seating, and improved drainage systems to prevent waterlogging would greatly enhance the passenger experience, especially during the rainy season.

In conclusion, while the MSRTC Shivneri Bus Stand in Dadar excels in terms of service efficiency, cleanliness, and staff courtesy, it falls short in providing basic facilities to protect passengers from adverse weather conditions. Addressing these issues will ensure that passengers have a comfortable and pleasant experience, regardless of the weather.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst Theatre. No management at all. Today parking was not available and when asked outside to the security guard person informed to park on the road and when asked if traffic person toe my vehicle than he said we are not responsible. I went up to the 3rd floor. Manager Ravi, I asked him about this and he is not even aware that parking is not available and need to park at the road... I don't know who made him the manager.

Easily the worst theater experience I’ve had. Zero management. Security told us to park on the street and explicitly said they weren’t responsible if our vehicle got towed. The manager, Ravi, was clueless about the parking situation and shouldn't be in his position. To top it off, they don't enforce age ratings—multiple families with kids were allowed into a restricted movie. When confronted, the staff was incredibly rude. Avoid this place at all costs.

Better go for Odeon or Rcity.. they are best in terms of staff behavior and parking.

"Ravi" first of all get some training on how to talk with customers.

featured_reviews.name: Mr.Khachack
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Rajhansh Cinema in Ghatkopar. The movie ticket was ₹300, which is fine, but the theatre quality honestly didn’t match the price. The projector seemed dull and outdated, which really affects the viewing experience.
I also bought food from the counter — ₹200 for fries that were even smaller than a McDonald's small fries, and a pizza for ₹250 that was quite small and average in taste. Overall, the food felt overpriced for the quantity and quality provided.
I hope they improve the theatre experience and food value, especially considering the prices they charge.
